subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 25, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 25, 2026

Good morning from Spokane! The AcreetionOS team is pushing forward with another productive week of refinements and upstream tracking. Natalie and Darren have been busy squashing UI bugs and polishing the installer experience for our growing community. We're excited to share what's been happening across development, the broader Arch ecosystem, and a few handy tips for your daily driver.

On the development front, Darren resolved the stubborn bottom-bar icon clickability issue across both the main AcreetionOS repository and the XLibre variant. This fix restores expected panel behavior that some users noticed after recent Cinnamon updates. The welcome screen also received attention with missing assets restored and layout inconsistencies cleaned up for a smoother first-boot experience.

Natalie initialized the new acreetionos-wallpapers repository, laying groundwork for a curated collection of original artwork that will ship with future ISO releases. Meanwhile, the XLibre integration continues to mature with another round of fixes pushed to the dedicated repository. These incremental improvements keep our graphics stack modern while maintaining the stability Arch users expect.

Infrastructure work continues behind the scenes as Darren maintains the GitLab CI pipelines and ISO build automation that keep releases shipping on schedule. The package list was trimmed this week with exfat-utils removed in favor of the modern exfatprogs implementation, aligning with upstream Arch packaging decisions. This kind of housekeeping keeps our images lean and our upgrade paths clean.

In community news, Firefox 161.0 landed this week with its usual blend of performance improvements, security hardening, and web platform enhancements. As the default browser in AcreetionOS, this update will flow through to users on their next system refresh. The Mozilla team continues to deliver a browser that respects user choice and open standards.

Security-conscious users should note that AlmaLinux issued two rounds of updates this week covering a wide surface area including curl, flatpak, kernel, golang, and container tooling. While AcreetionOS follows Arch's rolling model rather than AlmaLinux's release cycle, these advisories often signal upstream fixes that reach our repositories quickly. Staying current with pacman -Syu remains the best defense.

CachyOS announced their November 2026 release, showcasing the continued innovation happening across the Arch derivative ecosystem. Their performance-focused optimizations and kernel tuning experiments often inform broader community discussions. It's encouraging to see multiple healthy projects building on the same solid foundation.

This week's tip: if you're still referencing exfat-utils in scripts or package lists, migrate to exfatprogs — the legacy package has been dropped from Arch's repositories entirely. The new toolset offers better performance, active maintenance, and full feature parity for exFAT filesystem management. A quick pacman -Qs exfat will reveal any lingering dependencies worth updating.

That wraps up today's update — thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS journey. Join us on Discord or GitLab if you want to contribute, report issues, or just hang out with fellow Arch enthusiasts. Until tomorrow, keep your kernels fresh and your dotfiles versioned.
